reviews.title: So helpful for sleep patterns
reviews.contents: I’ve never written a review but my experience using Napper, as well as my customer service experience, have been exceptional. I’d been using two baby sleep apps for comparison, but Napper has out-performed the other (called Baby Naps). Napper allows me to track time spent nursing, diaper changes, medicine, naps, nighttime sleep and even night wakings. The predictive nap & sleep recommendations are extremely helpful, and rather than be prescriptive or static, the recommendations adjust according to when my baby sleeps, and for how long. (I imagine this is based on wake windows for the child’s age). I also really like the “nursing” module which has a stopwatch function and helps you record from which breast you fed from, and for how long. The logs are easy to edit and easy to access when you’re one-handed…When I wrote to their customer service team regarding a bug, Esper replied quickly with excellent feedback and was so helpful (thanks!). My husband and I are first time parents and really recommend trying Napper.

reviews.title: Almost perfect!
reviews.contents: I am still in the trial period and I was hopeful it would be THE ONE for tracking my 3 week old’s sleep and nursing. Unfortunately, I really dislike the editing capabilities for nursing. If I pause a nursing session but don’t unpause right away when we restart, I can’t go back and edit that pause. So then if I try to edit the nursing time on the L or R side to correct the time, it won’t allow me to without completely deleting the pause, which then throws the whole nursing session off. Being able to note the time I restarted and edit the nursing session when my hands are free once again should really be made possible. Moms can’t always hit start immediately or should be able sometimes forget to for a fee minutes while still having the ability to have accurate time kept. That’s my only gripe with this app and since nursing is half of the reason I really use this tracker, it’s a big deal for me. For that reason, I probably won’t even complete the trial period, but I wish I could! The sleep tracking is awesome but if I’m paying for an app I need to be able to track his nursing in the same place. — if the app developers change this I would totally recommend and would purchase it!

reviews.title: Good for sleep, not so good for tracking
reviews.contents: The app is good, it’s spot on with the timing for naps. It’s not magic, our baby still wakes up many times through the night but is understandable as babies go through many things that will make their sleep challenging. I’m giving two stars not because the sleep tracking but because of the bugs and interface. - I love the graph that shows the day and night ahead but you make the effort of tracking everything and then the nice interface disappear and you can’t see how the night went again with the nice graph and only with the historical one which is awful. The sleep is split in two days and so hard to know what is for what night. - Tracking night wakings and things in general is difficult when you or your partner did it and you’re out of sync. You end up duplicating or missing things. - It’s also a mess using the widgets again keeping them in sync with your partner's. Most of the time they’re not up to date and you know the baby was put to sleep and he has a night waking you use the widget and it is not the waking what you did but another sleep and the app accepts it without complaining. - is not clear what you’ll do when clicking the widget. I’ll give 5 stars when those issues are fixed, but those are pretty big issues for me.

reviews.title: It helped me so much!!
reviews.contents:
As a tired first time mom of a new baby. I struggled with keeping track of how long baby slept for at night, how long his naps were, wake window time frames and figuring what time to put him down for a nap if he woke up early from his previous nap. We were struggling! Baby always seemed over tired and fussy.
I was using huckleberry app but i didnt like how complicated it was and it was expensive, i needed something simple that focused mainly on sleep. I also appreciated that i can document bottle and pumping times too. I started using this app, within two weeks my baby went from waking up 5 times a night to once a night. Once we figured out his wake windows, then he slept through the night. Since 4 months old my baby has slept 12-13 hours.
I recommend this app to all parents struggling with sleep!
My baby is 7 months and i still use the app everyday!

reviews.title: No edit option after midnight
reviews.contents:
Edited to address the developer feedback to be clear. Unable to use any longer without paying, so I can’t further explore how it could possibly be edited. But I tried many times in the history tab to much frustration - and I think I’m a relatively tech savvy person. From what I could see you are able to edit entries, but for example if your baby falls asleep for the night at 11:55pm but you don’t add until 12am, you are unable to go into the history tab and add that they fell asleep for the night at that time (again from what I could figure out). You can edit for example a specific nap entry. But when you click the add button, and enter a time in the past day, it believes you mean the future and gives an error. Highly suggest adding a date feature in with the time to make everything more easily editable in the past.

OP: Loved this in real time, but honestly who can remember to mark every single thing the second it happens? Once midnight rolls around there seems to be zero ability to go to the day before and mark when your child went to sleep. We are parents, sleep doesn’t reset at midnight. So confused by this!

reviews.title: Wake windows way too long
reviews.contents: I had the napper app (paid version) for a couple months for my 5-6 month old to get a handle on her naps because we were struggling with short naps and getting the last nap in everyday. It said that it was 100 percent accurate and that it had learned her sleep cycles enough to make her ideal schedule, so this isn’t a review of the first few weeks using it. This app suggested her morning wake window be 3 hours long (which is too long for her) and then she’d only nap 35 min. Her second wake window would be like 3 hours and 45 mins. (Again, too long) giving us a short second nap and when it would suggest a third nap time- it would be so late in the day, putting her bed time a couple hours later than it should be. So if we’d skip the nap, the app would only change her bedtime by like 15 mins, suggesting her last wake window be up to 6 hours long. For a 6 month old!! I finally stopped using it, gave much shorter wake windows, and we are now getting 1-2 hour long naps regularly capping wake windows at 3-3.5 hours in the evening. Don’t waste your time or money.

reviews.title: Great until regressions
reviews.contents:
I saw a lot of recommendations for this app on reddit so I decided to give it a shot. For regular sleep patterns this thing is eerily accurate but if your LO deviates at all due to the insanely long list of reasons -  teething, sickness, separation anxiety, etc or an inevitable sleep regression, the suggestions will be off track and sometimes really off because it’s still going off wake windows. I had downloaded it originally as I was desperate to figure out how to get through a regression but it’s not the app for that. For example when my LO has a EMW I wanted good guidance for when they should nap next which based on my hours of research online (baby sleep can do that to you) but it’ll suggest the nap based off your LO’s typically wake window which isn’t ideal in these situations.

Despite my feedback I truly enjoy the UI and still use it to track sleep. My favorite is the ability to add pauses to naps which my other apps do not have. I do have faith that the app will continue to improve though. Hope this helps

reviews.title: Underrated
reviews.contents:
At first I though this app was just like all the others saying it would help you out with finding your babies schedule but I have to say that this one is on a whole different level than the others.

The first day of course the app is not up to speed on your baby and their schedules. But after just a couple of days the app has learned when and how long my baby sleeps. It’s really accurate and detailed. My husband and I were in awe as we saw our baby getting sleepy around the time the app would say it’s time for his nap. At first we were skeptical but we noticed our babies sleepy cues and realized it was on time.

We’ve continued to use it in comparison to an other app I was using and Napper is by far so much easier for me and my partner to use. It even give you the option to share the same info with another person so my partner has access to all the same things I do on his phone. 

I have loved the app so much I have stopped using the one I had before( Baby tracker ). I highly recommend this app for first time parents like myself. 

But I will say, if this isn’t for you then do not force it. Mothers, you know your baby best, so do not believe that you have to stick with something if it doesn’t work out for you and baby. Trust your own instincts. You got this

reviews.title: Thank you for saving these FTParents sanity
reviews.contents:
Dear developers of Napper,

Thank you so much for saving us our sanity. Sleep deprived from having an intense contact Napper the past 4 months, we were doing our best to keep up with the new wake times and the next set of googled schedules we could fine online and educate ourselves on the appropriate wake times.

Obviously getting your baby to adhere to some random schedule found on Google is hard. Every baby is so different and so is every day. Some naps are skipped and some naps are cut shorter because someone sneezed too loud or God forbid dropped a hydroflask on the floor. 

That being said, finding Napper on some obscure Instagram comment from a mom saved us. Napper legit adjusts to your baby's schedule and predicts the next nap/bedtime. Also your day is so busy, it gives you a 30 mins heads up to be mindful and it's been so accurate from day 2 of logging in data. 

Napper's also design just makes sense. As a visual person it's awesome to see the whole day as an arc. We were super users of Glow baby and it felt sort of pointless at logging into a linear abyss. At least with Napper you can glance at it and understand how to structure your day based on the predicted naps. WHICH IS A GODSEND when you have limited time and  energy.

Anyways. Thank you. It was worth taking the time to write this review because its saved my mental headspace. It was so freeing deleting the scheduled blocks on my Google calendar. Thank you 😭

If there's anything I'd like to see- can yall have a lifetime price instead of a subscription model? 😂 thank you 

TL;DR - Napper adjusts the naps to your baby, not the other way around like every dinosaur method out there.

reviews.title: Almost perfect
reviews.contents: Found this app specifically for tracking a sleep and very happy with it.. almost. I like the interface: the clock that gives you a full picture of the day or night with some sleep frame suggestions (not always correct for your child, but definitely by the standards). You can track naps and night wakes up separately. I wish we can swipe the clock as well between days and nights, instead of always going back to history and swiping there. But one star down for me is for the glitch. I’ve been using the app for a little longer than a month and had to reinstall it at least 5 times.. sometimes interface just says hold on and no clock will appear.. one time it messed the day and night sleep and the whole history, the other time it just won’t open.. I hope it will be fixed soon, because so far I like this app best from all others.
